PASSAGE VI
AI-Assisted Judging: A Gold Medal Idea
The athletic feats performed at the Olympics
never cease to amaze me. A snowboarder corkscrews
through the sky. A leaping figure skater lands perfectly
on one foot. Two divers simultaneously spring from their
parallel boards. As a casual enthusiast, I often struggle
to distinguish the great performances, from the merely
good. For Olympic judges, though, the slight differences
matter—a lot. [
A
] Unfortunately, even these experts
can miss an error separating a performance
earning a nine point five from a coveted ten.
Suppose the writer’s primary purpose had been to
compare methods of survival used by two plant species
native to Scandinavia. Would this essay accomplish
that purpose?
F.
Yes, because it lists the various defenses shared
by mountain birch trees and marsh Labrador tea
plants in Finland.
G.
Yes, because it demonstrates how two plant
species unique to Scandinavia can have a similar
genetic makeup despite differences in height.
H.
No, because it focuses instead on natural ways to
repel herbivores based on cultural practices that
are rooted in ancient Scandinavian folklore.
J.
No, because it focuses instead on the beneficial
relationship between two plant species by
explaining how they protect themselves from
herbivores.
Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically
acceptable?
A. No Change
B.
enthusiast, I often struggle to distinguish the great
performances
C.
enthusiast I often struggle to distinguish the great
performances,
D.
enthusiast I often struggle to distinguish the great
performances
